title: Task-Focused Summarization of Email
research_question: Can a system identify task-bearing sentences in email and reformulate them into a task-focused summary that supports adding items to a to-do list?
methodology: SmartMail separates new message bodies from headers and forwarded text, classifies body sentences as Task/non-Task with a linear SVM trained by sequential minimal optimization, and studies feature ablations using message, surface, and NLPWin linguistic features. Gold uses single speech-act labels, with majority labels and whole-message disagreement filtering for development/blind test. It evaluates sentence and derived message precision–recall curves, illustrates rule-based logical-form reformulation, and demonstrates Outlook interfaces; reformulation/user studies remain future work.

key_findings.finding: Gold annotation assigns one speech-act tag per message-body sentence; Task means a suitable ongoing to-do item and usually excludes simple factual questions. Annotators use whole-message context for ambiguous formulaic requests.
key_findings.quote: Annotators were instructed to mark a sentence as containing a task if it looked like an appropriate item to add to an on-going “to do” list. By this criterion, simple factual questions would not usually be annotated as tasks; merely responding with an answer fulfills any obligation. Annotators

key_findings.finding: On the blind email test set, the authors report that all features give the best sentence-level Task-versus-non-Task precision–recall results in approximate recall ranges 0.2–0.4 and 0.5–0.6; the two linguistic-feature ablations differ negligibly.
key_findings.quote: Figure 1 shows final results for these feature sets on the blind test set: for recall between approximately 0.2 and 0.4 and between approximately 0.5 and 0.6 the use of all features produces the best results. The distinction between the “no linguistic features” and “no deep linguistic features” scenarios is negligible; word n-grams appear to be highly predictive.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Empirical curves and author interpretation; no significance test, exact point table, or fixed-threshold score.

key_findings.finding: Using all features, flagging a message when any sentence is predicted Task gives a higher precision–recall curve than sentence-level classification; this is evidence about finding at least one task, not recovering every task.

key_findings.finding: The prototype offers task checkboxes, original-message links, in-context highlighting, and a classifier threshold slider; user studies of usefulness and reformulation variants remain planned.
key_findings.quote: We plan to conduct user studies by distributing the prototype as an Outlook add-in to volunteers who would use it to read and process their own mail over a period of several weeks. We intend to measure more than the precision and recall of our classifier by observing how many identified tasks users actually add to their “to do” list and by administering qualitative surveys of user satisfaction.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Interface description and future study plan, not measured workload reduction or preservation.

key_findings.finding: The authors expect that omitting deeper linguistic features will retain good classification performance in languages without an NLPWin parser, but report no cross-language evaluation.
key_findings.quote: Based on these results, we expect that for languages where we do not have an NLPWin parser, we can safely exclude the deeper linguistic features and still expect good classifier performance.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Expectation extrapolated from the reported email ablation; no multilingual result.

limitations: The narrow Task label usually excludes factual questions requiring only an answer; it is not a comprehensive obligation label (D08-F01).
No Topic identities, Topic segmentation, exact-span gold, multi-membership, overlap, or discontinuous semantic-object evaluation (E01/E02/E06/E09).
Heading-to-task assignee scope is explicitly reported as not detected (D08-F07); no preservation metrics assess reformulation (D08-F05).
Corpus source population and language inventory are unspecified; mostly Outlook usage and rare inline interleaving limit demonstrated coverage (E02).
No positive-class/test-sentence counts, detailed hyperparameters, exact curve points, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests (E03/E05/E06/E07).
Consensus filtering may omit difficult messages; sender separation does not demonstrate thread/duplicate isolation (E02/E03, analyst inference).
No completed user study, measured reading-effort reduction, or task-reformulation preference results (D08-F08).
Retain original enumeration, metric-wording, and corpus-accounting issues D08-I01–I03.

reproducibility.implementation: Linear SVM/SMO, approximate feature inventory, NLPWin, LF rewrite steps, and split policy are described. Code, exact trained parameters, preprocessing implementation, model selection detail, and full annotation guide are not supplied.

confidence_interpretation: Confidence in faithful extraction and evidence qualification, not probability of operational success. Unsupported method descriptions and limitations are source-grounded but not experimentally evaluated under the installed contract.
raw_claims: We collected a corpus of 15,741 email messages.
Annotators were instructed to mark a sentence as containing a task if it looked like an appropriate item to add to an on-going “to do” list.
Each sentence in the message body is described by a vector of approximately 53,000 features.
All parts of the logical form not subsumed by the task clause are pruned.
SmartMail does not currently detect this explicit assignment of tasks to individuals.

annotation_unit.unit: Message-body sentence; one application-specific speech-act tag. Whole-message context informs interpretation. No clause/span/EDU boundary gold is described.

prediction_unit.unit: Binary Task label per sentence; derived binary flag per message. Subsequent rules select a clause or whole sentence in a logical form and generate task text. No exact character-offset assignment is evaluated.

contiguity.status: Sentence classification followed by a list of independently extracted tasks. No contiguous Topic segmentation or non-sequential Topic clustering.
contiguity.scope: A list may contain separated sentences from one message; this does not establish that they support one semantic object.

label_cardinality.gold: Exactly one speech-act tag per annotated sentence, including the default None of the above; no multiple Topic memberships. A message can contain multiple Task sentences, without separate work-matter identities.
label_cardinality.prediction: One binary Task/non-Task decision per sentence at a chosen threshold; one contains-Task flag per message. No multilabel span or message Topic predictions.

gold.within_one_message: No annotation linking non-contiguous spans to one task or Topic is reported.
gold.thread_level: No gold linkage of tasks/Topics across messages is reported.

prediction.within_one_message: Separated task sentences can be selected, but no identity relation combines discontinuous spans as one task/Topic. Logical-form pruning is not a discontinuous Topic-span representation.
prediction.thread_level: No task/Topic cluster prediction across messages; header/body/forward separation is preprocessing only.

overlap.gold: The stated single-tag sentence scheme does not encode overlapping task or Topic spans. No gold multi-membership or nested assignment reported.
overlap.prediction: No overlapping task/Topic span assignment described or evaluated.
overlap.scope: Neither multiple tasks per email nor sender-heading scope establishes overlapping Topic membership.

dataset_domain.name: Unnamed collected email corpus
dataset_domain.paper_reported: Email; most senders used Microsoft Outlook, and interleaving of quoted original messages with new content was extremely uncommon.
dataset_domain.not_reported: Sampling dates, organizational population, domain breakdown, and corpus language inventory. English examples are visible, but no language proportions are reported.

annotation_process.procedure: Three annotators label sentences using one tag from Salutation, Chit-chat, Task, Meeting, Promise, Farewell, Sig_Name, Sig_Title, Sig_Affiliation, Sig_Location, Sig_Phone, Sig_Email, Sig_URL, Sig_Other, and None of the above. Task excludes most simple factual questions. Context distinguishes social formulae from requests for review/comment.
annotation_process.test_gold: All three annotate development and blind test. Majority sentence tag is gold. If any sentence has no majority, the entire message is discarded.
annotation_process.training_gold: The paper states that three annotators labeled the corpus but does not specify independent coverage or adjudication for each training sentence.

inter_annotator_agreement.metric: Pairwise Cohen’s Kappa; the paper reports percentage notation, not raw percent agreement.
inter_annotator_agreement.population: All speech-act sentence tags in 146 separate messages excluded from training, development, and blind test; number of sentences not reported.
inter_annotator_agreement.not_reported: Task-only Kappa, span agreement, uncertainty labels, confidence intervals, and agreement on work-matter identity.

split_and_leakage.split_unit: Messages allocated with all mail from each sender in training or test, to test previously unseen senders. Whether development and blind test are mutually sender-disjoint is not stated.
split_and_leakage.controls: Sender cap and train/test sender separation are reported. Thread grouping, temporal split, duplicate/near-duplicate filtering, quoted-content deduplication, and cross-sender thread leakage controls are not reported.
split_and_leakage.missing: Development/blind sentence counts, positive Task counts at both units, pre-filter test counts, discarded-message counts, seed, and detailed split membership.
split_and_leakage.interpretation: Whole-message removal on any unresolved label can select a less ambiguous test population; no quantified effect is reported. Sender separation alone does not establish thread or content independence.

metrics.definition: Standard interpretation: precision = true Task sentences / predicted Task sentences; recall = true Task sentences / gold Task sentences. Formulas are not explicitly printed.
metrics.dataset_task_split: Unnamed email corpus; binary sentence Task detection; final Figure 1 blind test, 699 retained messages; sentence and positive-class denominators not reported.
metrics.setting: Linear SVM trained with sequential minimal optimization. Approximately 53,000 features per sentence in the full description: message, surface n-grams/punctuation/name cues, and NLPWin linguistic features. Development ablations determine run-time feature selection; explicit final selected configuration and SVM hyperparameters are not fully specified.
metrics.results: D08-F03; all-features, no-deep-linguistic-features, and no-linguistic-features curves. Exact plotted coordinates, F1, AUC, precision at a fixed recall, recall at a fixed precision, and statistical tests are not reported as numeric tables.

metrics.definition: Standard interpretation: precision = correctly flagged Task-containing messages / predicted Task-containing messages; recall = correctly flagged Task-containing messages / gold Task-containing messages. A predicted message is positive if any sentence is predicted Task. Gold message construction is implied by contains-task evaluation but not separately formalized.
metrics.dataset_task_split: Same email study; Figure 2 with all features. Blind test is the surrounding final-results context, but the Figure 2 paragraph/caption does not explicitly restate its split or message count. Do not treat a Figure 2 denominator of 699 as independently confirmed.
metrics.results: D08-F04; higher message-level curve. No exact numeric performance points or class counts. The prose term accuracy is not a reported scalar accuracy metric.

metrics.dataset_task_split: Separate annotation-agreement set, all speech-act sentence tags, 146 messages; not model evaluation.

measured_work_text_preservation.plausible_risk: Analyst interpretation: clause, modifier, or modality pruning can remove decision-bearing conditions/evidence or broaden action scope. documented_text_transformations.evidence_kind: Documented text transformation; qualitative source input/output example

source_input.quote: On the H-1 visa issue, I am positive that you need to go to the Embassy in London to get your visa stamped into your passport.

source_output.quote: Go to the Embassy in London to get your visa stamped into your passport.

source_explanation.quote: In this example, the embedded sentential complement, that is, the part of the sentence following positive, is selected as the part of the sentence containing the task, because of the modal verb need and the second person subject; only that part of the sentence gets reformulated. The modal verb and the second person subject are deleted to form an imperative sentence.

observed_changes: The displayed output omits the explicit context 'On the H-1 visa issue' and the sender's assertion of confidence 'I am positive'.
The source explains that the embedded complement is selected and the modal verb need and second-person subject are deleted to form an imperative.
The output retains going to the Embassy in London and the purpose of getting the recipient's visa stamped into the recipient's passport.
documented_text_transformations.fidelity_judgment: No paired gold semantic-fidelity judgment is supplied. The displayed omissions are not automatically classified as semantic errors.
documented_text_transformations.aggregate_preservation_metric: Not reported; this one example supplies no aggregate preservation denominator or rate.
documented_text_transformations.conditional_clause_boundary: Example 1 does not demonstrate deletion of a conditional clause. The general rule mentions pruning subordinate clauses; that alone cannot establish an observed conditional-deletion error. The conditional task sentence in §2 (raw lines 143–146, PDF p. 2) is not paired with a reformulation.

interpretation.statement: Task is narrower than msgloom work needing a response. A classifier that reproduces this gold could correctly exclude a factual question while missing work important to msgloom. This is a target-definition mismatch, not a measured model error.
A message flag can remain correct while additional actions or their scope are missed. Its superior curve cannot validate complete work coverage or Topic span assignment.
The missed heading scope motivates testing context beyond a sentence, but does not establish sentence, clause, EDU, arbitrary-span, or hybrid superiority.

Keep source extraction and optional rewriting separately assessable. The fallback and links preserve access to source text, but access alone does not prove that a summary retained all decision-bearing meaning.
